subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should OpenClaw publish `inbound_debounce` as a stable cross-channel plugin SDK contract, or should conversation-specific WhatsApp debounce remain a channel configuration feature?
rationale: Both approaches can solve the linked use case, but choosing the permanent public API and avoiding competing policy sources requires maintainer ownership rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Sponsor the plugin hook
options.body: Approve the generic hook direction, define its stable arbitration and failure contract, and require a real plugin-driven WhatsApp proof before merge.

options.title: Prefer channel configuration
options.body: Continue with the narrower configuration approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 and avoid publishing a new general plugin hook.

options.title: Pause both approaches
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open until maintainers define the supported debounce customization boundary across channels.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the plugin hook
recommendation.body: Approve the generic hook direction, define its stable arbitration and failure contract, and require a real plugin-driven WhatsApp proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily about the shared plugin hook API rather than the mechanics of the WhatsApp adapter.
